description:
FILED s467 (Fable, 2026-09-04), found by the README demo program (a `local $, = "-"; print 1 .. 5` line printed 12345).

Minimal repro, all spellings probed vs perl 5.40.3:
  use feature "signatures"; local $, = "-"; print 1,2,3;   perl 1-2-3   PCL 123  (SILENT)
  use v5.36;                local $, = "-"; print 1,2,3;   perl 1-2-3   PCL 123  (SILENT)
  use feature "signatures"; $, = "-"; print 1,2,3;         perl 1-2-3   PCL DROP: "statement dropped ... $, = \"-\"; -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case: []"
  use v5.36;                $, = "-"; print 1,2,3;         perl 1-2-3   PCL DROP (same)
  (no signatures feature)   local $, = "-"; print 1,2,3;   perl 1-2-3   PCL 1-2-3  -- correct
  use feature "signatures"; local $" = ":"; local $; = "|"; print "$,|"   -- all correct: it is `$,` alone

The trigger is the FEATURE being in force, not a sub with a signature: `use feature "signatures"` + `local $,` with no sub in the file reproduces it.  A sub with a signature inside a `package NAME {}` block is only how the demo met it.

Emission (pl2cl, gen v2-611): the local form is `(let (($ (p-box-for-local "-"))) (p-print 1 2 3) ...)` -- the symbol should be `|$,|` (that is what the non-signature tree emits) but the comma is gone, so the let binds a fresh variable `$` and p-print reads the untouched `pcl::|$,|`.  The plain assignment falls through the statement classifier with an EMPTY missing-case list (`Missing case: []`), i.e. the token stream handed on has nothing where `$,` stood.

SUSPECT (not verified -- the cheap discriminating measurement is dumping the token stream after the #455 signature-region repair): the repair that decides a `(...)` after `sub NAME` is a Structure::Signature vs a Token::Prototype when the feature is in force (`_signatures_enabled_at`, s438e), or the `proto_text_has_named_params` / `_signature_param_canons` split on TOP-LEVEL COMMAS, treats the Magic token `$,` as `$` + `,` -- a comma-splitter running over a token whose TEXT is `$,`.  Grep for the comma split in Pl/Parser.pm and Pl/Parser2.pm first (rule 11: find the one place).

Why it matters: `use v5.36` is the modern boilerplate, and `$,` / `$\` are common in one-liners and report scripts.  A SILENT loss of the separator is the worst shape of the #138 family.

Bar for the fix: Pl/ change -> gate + corpus-diff (expect IDENTICAL unless a corpus file uses `$,` under signatures) + emission-ab lib; guard rows (Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t or a punctuation-variable guard): the spellings above, `$,` interpolated, `$,` under `use v5.36`, and the inverse (no feature) unchanged.
subject: SILENT WRONG: under `use feature "signatures"` (so also `use v5.36`+) the output-field separator `$,` is mis-tokenized -- `local $, = "-"` binds a variable named `$` (the separator is silently lost) and `$, = "-"` is DROPPED; the other punctuation variables probed ($" $; $\) are fine
